paragraphs: Rav Yirmeya of Difta. Hyman writes that he was one of Rava's students, as in [Zevachim 34b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.34b.14): Ravina said to Rav Ashi, 'Rav Yirmeya of Difti taught in Rava’s name.' Hyman also says he received teachings from Rav Papa and Rav Pappi, as in [Bava Kamma 73a:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.73a.4) and [Sanhedrin 27a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.27a.6), where he said that Rav Papa acted in accordance with Rava; and in [Shabbat 109b:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.109b.5) he said that Rav Pappi's view seems more reasonable; and in [Avodah Zarah 40a:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.40a.7) he said:

'Rav Pappi said to me.' We also find that he challenged Rav Kahana (the teacher of Rav Ashi), as in [Bava Batra 171b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.171b.15). And we find in [Megillah 18b](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.18b.14) 'Rami bar Chama said to him,' but Hyman calls that a scribal error, since Rami bar Chama died long before Rava; Hyman says it should read Rami bar Berachya, as in the reading he cites from דק״ס. And in [Zevachim 34b:4-5](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.34b.4-5) he disagrees with Rav Zevid.

And in [Chullin 87b:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.87b.9) he disagrees with R. Assi of Neharbel. Hyman considers him older than Ravina, as in Kiddushin 33b, where Ravina was sitting before him, and in [Yoma 42a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.42a.3) he answered Ravina: they do not disagree about the cow but about the scapegoat. They also debated as colleagues in [Yevamot 8a:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.8a.7) and [Yevamot 54a:19](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.54a.19). And in [Zevachim 34b:14](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.34b.14) Ravina said to Rav Ashi, 'Thus said Rav Yirmeya [ר״י] of Difta', and so it should read there at 15b,

and there it reads 'Rav Yirmeya' but Hyman proposes 'Ravina,' as in the reading of דק״ס. And in [Menachot 31b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.31b.2) Rabbah Zuta said to Rav Ashi, 'Thus said Rav Yirmeya of Difta.' He is further mentioned in Shabbat 22a [translator note: supplied שכת כב., read as שבת; supplied form preserved] (according to the reading of the [Sheiltot d'Rav Achai Gaon 26:4-5](https://www.sefaria.org/Sheiltot_d'Rav_Achai_Gaon.26.4-5)), ער. פב. קנה: [see the parallels at [Shabbat 82a:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.82a.6) and [Shabbat 155b:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.155b.4)], [Eruvin 24a:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.24a.4), [Yoma 63a:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.63a.16), [Nedarim 22b:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.22b.2), [Avodah Zarah 22b:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.22b.12), [Chullin 35b:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.35b.2) (where he challenges Rava's words).
Hyman also cites Eruvin 43b for Rav Menashya son of Yirmeya of Difti, according to the reading of ע״י.[^7][^8]

notes.text: Hyman's abbreviation ער. is not expanded; it is retained literally and unresolved.
ע״י is unknown and kept in Hebrew without guessing; דק״ס is rendered Dikdukei Soferim as a conventional expansion, not from the registry (empty), so uncertain.
Colon rendered as amud b and period as amud a in suggested refs only; printed labels preserved. Hyman's identification of the Megillah reading as a scribal error is his editorial claim.

Whole source/current English/all historical notes and earlier model decisions read. Hyman owns teacher/student and relative-age reconstructions and proposed RamiBarBerachya/Ravina corrections; no scribal-history proof. ר״י ofDifta is contextually RavYirmeya from the full heading and repeated name in this very source; empty registry alone is not a reason to withhold an otherwise explicit contextual expansion. Difta/Difti forms remain distinct. דק״ס remains disclosed; ער. פב. קנה: and ע״י are still unresolved and held. Supplied שכת and the contextual Shabbat rendering remain disclosed; no new printed-pixel check. All inherited substantive notes retained, with their obsolete empty-registry restriction qualified here. References to printed/native readings in inherited notes are preserved historical claims; this root pass uses supplied digital text and named saved editions, not a fresh pixel or correction-history verification.

A bounded check of Davidson Eruvin43b did not locate the supplied Menashya/Yirmeya-of-Difti phrase. Hyman explicitly conditions his citation on the reading of ע״י; checking a different named edition cannot establish or refute that specific witness, and the siglum remains unresolved. The complete nineteen-paragraph Davidson Eruvin 43b page was read for that bounded comparison. The three whole selected Davidson Zevachim 34b paragraphs have Rav Zevid and Rav Yirmeya of Difti transmitting separate versions, and Ravina reporting Rav Yirmeya of Difti in the name of Rava to Rav Ashi. They support that reporting direction, not a new teacher relationship or proof of Hyman’s relative-age reconstruction. His Rami bar Chama/Rami bar Berachya and Rav Yirmeya/Ravina corrections, chronology, and other uncollated citations remain his claims. The source’s full Rav titles and contextual Yirmeya expansion are retained; R. Assi remains the supplied abbreviated title. Difta/Difti, שכת, ער. פב. קנה:, and ע״י remain distinct or unresolved as supplied. The four existing notes remain verbatim, with no new retirement, Hebrew repair, identity binding, or held publication.

Davidson Zevachim 34b distinguishes the versions recited by Rav Zevid and Rav Yirmeya of Difti and has Ravina report Yirmeya in Rava’s name to Rav Ashi. At 15b Rabbi Yirmeya reports Rav Yirmeya of Difti to Rav Ashi. Megillah 18b has Rami bar Chama. Hyman’s proposed Ravina and Rami bar Berachya readings and his chronological arguments remain attributed to him. Hyman’s printed notice (II, pp. 815–816) has שבת where the supplied witness has שכת. In Davidson Shabbat 22a the lamp discussion names Rav Shmuel of Difti. Vilna Sheiltot 26 names Rabbi Yirmeya of Difti in a parallel discussion, without assigning the right and left positions to named speakers in those clauses. Shabbat 82a and 155b both independently name Rav Yirmeya of Difti. These are parallels at the two supplied folio numbers, with ער. still unexpanded. Hyman’s printed Eruvin locator for Menashya is 43b. Glick’s Ein Yaakov has Menashya son of Rabbi Yirmeya of Difti under folio 64, while the Daat Ein Yaakov and Davidson Eruvin 64a have mi-Gifti. The Glick reading supplies the matching patronymic at another locus. Hyman’s edition and the exact expansion of ע״י remain unverified, and the parallel does not establish the father’s identity.

Zevachim 34b gives Rav Zevid’s and Yirmeya’s versions and has Ravina transmit Yirmeya’s ruling in Rava’s name. Zevachim 15b instead names Rabbi Yirmeya as the reporter. Megillah names Rami bar Chama. Heilprin’s parallel notice gives the same named reporter in Zevachim 15b and cites Rami bar Chama. Sanhedrin 27a names Rav Pappi where the supplied Hebrew says Rav Papa. See also [Zevachim 34b (the two versions)](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.34b.4-5), [Zevachim 15b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.15b.2). See [Heilprin’s parallel discussion](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2239&lang=en).

[Avodah Zarah 40a:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.40a.7) gives Yirmeya quoting what Rav Pappi told him. [Zevachim 34b:4-5](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.34b.4-5) records the versions taught by Rav Zevid and Yirmeya. The episode of Ravina sitting before Yirmeya is at [Kiddushin 33a:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.33a.16). Hyman cites Kiddushin 33b. Both [Yevamot 8a:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.8a.7) and [Yevamot 54a:19](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.54a.19) name Rav Acha of Difti in dialogue with Ravina. [Sheiltot d'Rav Achai Gaon 26:4-5](https://www.sefaria.org/Sheiltot_d'Rav_Achai_Gaon.26.4-5) names Rabbi Yirmeya in the discussion of the placement of the Hanukkah lamp. [Chullin 35b:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.35b.2) names Yirmeya and presents his objection in the discussion of Rabbi Yitzchak’s position. [Ein Yaakov, Glick edition, Eruvin 64](https://or-breslev.co.il/library/%D7%A2%D7%99%D7%9F-%D7%99%D7%A2%D7%A7%D7%91-%D7%9E%D7%90%D7%AA-%D7%A9%D7%9E%D7%95%D7%90%D7%9C-%D7%A6%D7%91%D7%99-%D7%92%D7%9C%D7%99%D7%A7/%D7%A2%D7%99%D7%A8%D7%95%D7%91%D7%99%D7%9F/#l366) reads “Menashya son of Rabbi Yirmeya of Difti.” [Eruvin 64a:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.64a.10) reads “from Gifti.” Hyman’s Eruvin 43b and the siglum ע״י remain as supplied.
